refusals.head: cannot_hold_together
refusals.where: bars.json B1 (says 'clear-air openings beside the local Dark'; accept 1 'a warm open-air edge') with B2 reject 2, rule R1, census.json dark_field (kept as signature, 'outdoor drifting pockets') and tickets.md T31
refusals.evidence: R1 says ordinary local air temperature causes the Dark's density, and B2 reject 2 refuses the current Perlin offset. In RM_MapComponentDark.cs:68-71, unroofed cells read c.GetTemperature(map), which is the map's single outdoor temperature, and their only spatial variation is Mathf.PerlinNoise. RM_AbyssLight.cs:147 reads map.mapTemperature.OutdoorTemp directly. The two other things that open outdoor air, fold lanes and phantom pockets, both move to next version (T5, T16). So under R1 the outdoor Dark is uniform across the map at any moment: it clears or closes everywhere at once, and the only 'clear-air openings' left are heated roofed rooms. The proposal files this as an 'implementation risk' and an 'unsettled measurement' (definition.md, Physical boundaries; owner_pages.md page two) when it is a known engine fact that can be settled now.
refusals.would_pass: A definition that says now whether open-air pockets exist in 0.1.0. If they do, it says what produces them and how the player reads that cause, in a way R1 and B2 allow. If they don't, B1's pictures show the edge of a heated room or the map-wide opening and closing, not an outdoor warm edge.
refusals.smallest_fix: Move 'outdoor drifting pockets' to next_version (off) and restate R1: outdoor density follows the one outdoor temperature, and a room's density follows that room's temperature. Rewrite B1 accept 1 as 'a heated room's open doorway shows clear air against the Dark outside'. Put the choice on page two as a settled default.

refusals.head: kept_mechanic_undefined
refusals.where: census.json local_dark_presentation (needed_by 'signature and land'); bars.json B1 accept 2 ('returning ambient Dark conceals that view'); tickets.md T29; definition.md opening paragraph ('the air itself hides the country, nearby predators and your own lights')
refusals.evidence: No spatial Dark renderer exists (census dark_field: 'no spatial Dark renderer was located here'). T29 only says what the presentation must NOT hide (controls, selected pawns, readable danger signs). Nowhere is it defined what the Dark does hide or how: terrain only, buildings, unselected colonists, wild animals, hostile pawns; dimmed or removed from view. One builder makes a density-scaled tint. Another culls predator sprites in Dark cells, which is the 'conceals terrors close by' reading. Both pass B1 as written, and they are different mods.
refusals.would_pass: A definition of what the Dark visibly does to each class: terrain and relief, buildings, own pawns, wild animals and hostiles. Say whether anything is ever fully hidden from the player and what keeps a hidden predator readable. Add a B1 accept/reject pair that separates a tint from concealment.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add one paragraph to definition.md 'Physical boundaries' (e.g. 'the Dark darkens terrain and things in proportion to density; animals and hostiles inside it are drawn dimmed, never removed; own colonists stay fully drawn'). Add one B1 reject picture: 'a predator in the Dark is drawn exactly as in clear air'. Copy the rule into T29.

refusals.head: extra_without_argument
refusals.where: census.json nevarithia_halo and halo_release (fate 'signature', needed_by 'none: not a needed_by classification', built absent); bars.json B2 accept 2 and 3, R8; tickets.md T31 halo specification
refusals.evidence: RM_Nevarithia.xml:8-10: 'The walking knot of Dark and its release on death are OWED as our own mechanic ... not built here.' The signature sentence names living light, warmth, feeders and grain, not a creature carrying Dark. Without the halo the Dark → light/warmth → krizzak → grain chain works whole. frozen abyss.md:135 describes the beast ('halo of Dark around itself even where the Dark normally cannot form'). That says how the halo behaves if it exists, not that 0.1.0 must have it. The brief requires that an animal with a mechanic of its own stays only with a deletion argument. None is given, and this one is unbuilt new work: the opposite of 'smaller is how it passes'.
refusals.would_pass: Either a written deletion argument showing that removing the halo defeats land, life or the signature, or the halo and its death release moved to next version (off), with B2's pictures rewritten not to rely on it.
refusals.smallest_fix: Move nevarithia_halo and halo_release to next_version.md, keep nevarithia as ordinary life, and drop the halo part of T31 into a T10-style 'specify deferred promise' ticket. In B2, replace accept 2's second clause and accept 3's death-release clause with pictures that don't need a carried knot, and remove R8 or mark it next version.

refusals.head: core_promise_weakened
refusals.where: definition.md 'Why a player reaches for it' (claims to make concrete 'the owner's 2026-10-20 protection/nearby terror/brief beauty sentence'); owner_pages.md page one; bars.json B1/B8 meant
refusals.evidence: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md:7, the owner's words: 'Wonders emerge just as often for moments of transcendent beauty, only to twist into nightmares just as swiftly. You fear staying here too long will find the source of the nightmares themselves.' No bar carries a moment of beauty turning into danger: the Unveiling only clears and closes. Nothing carries the third sentence. The content that carried it (cryptid_dream after a long stay, cryptid sites, lore, phantom) all moves to next version in next_version.md. The definition says erosion 'already supplies the cost of staying', which is a material cost, not the dread of finding a source. Page one doesn't tell him that two of his three sentences are carried thinly or not at all.
refusals.would_pass: Each clause of his sentence is mapped to the bar that carries it, or stated plainly on page one as deferred to next version with the extras that carried it.
refusals.smallest_fix: On page one add one line: 'Your sentence's "twist into nightmares" and "staying too long … source of the nightmares" are deferred with the cryptid content' (or name the bar that carries each). In B1/B8 'meant', say which clause each bar carries.

refusals.head: figurative_unmarked
refusals.where: bars.json B7 says ('The player hears stillness broken by …'); B8 says ('runaway residue', 'cascading errors'); both have figurative: []
refusals.evidence: 'Hears stillness' cannot be held literally: stillness is an absence. Read literally it invites a build that mutes all environmental sound, and B7's left_out has to patch that afterwards ('ordinary colony/fire/combat sounds need not cease'). 'Runaway' and 'cascading' in B8 are figures for an accumulation and for repeated exceptions. The brief requires each such word to be marked, with an accept picture that departs from the literal reading.
refusals.would_pass: Each word listed in 'figurative' with what it stands for, plus one accept picture per word that departs from the literal reading.
refusals.smallest_fix: B7 figurative: 'stillness' = no steady wind bed between gusts, while ordinary colony and combat sounds continue (the existing accept 2 already serves as its picture). B8 figurative: 'runaway' = residue piling up faster than ordinary hauling and refining use it; 'cascading' = exceptions that repeat or spread after one fault.

stranger.text: A worker sees black etched crags above a dark-sand route and a warm open-air edge; living plants light the nearby ground while a workshop remains findable.
Unveiling shows the explored etched country; returning ambient Dark conceals that view while the maintained nearby light and selected pawn remain readable.
Fog art hides the selected worker and controls as completely as the distant country.
A flat black sand map and a uniformly dark sky contain all the named terrain labels but no etched standing relief or local air boundary.
A warm room loses the murk hediff but its shots still suffer the unchanged Abyss blanket penalty through entirely clear air.
The screen shows a clear pocket whose ordinary thermometer is still as cold as the opaque cell beside it, solely because an unseen effective-temperature noise offset was added.
An evacuated visitor leaves the biome and loses air-caused murk; a beast dying leaves a corpse and a visible local release that disperses in warm air.
An unheated work room has impaired visitor sight; ordinary heating clears its air and the same visitor can work and aim normally inside it.
A warm observer and a warm target separated by Dark still lack clean long-range targeting; a carried nevarithia knot remains locally opaque in otherwise clear ambient air.
A warm rooftop shooter gets clean aim across the gunk, or a dead/despawned beast leaves a permanent invisible halo.
Native plants are in the roster but their only wild establishment path needs sunlight or a pre-existing light cluster that cannot establish itself.
A plant looks luminous, but useful crop light never reaches the warmed growing cells.
Native grass supports grazing, tree mushroom supplies timber and paddle vine supplies workable ordinary fiber in the Dark; a wild light cluster can establish and regrow without imported sky light.

A transplanted wickwood or giant glow globe lights warmed crop ground; crops advance there while otherwise matched unlit crops do not. Native berries and hollow fungus yield edible food through ordinary harvest.
Etchcap grows on ordinary fertile sand as readily as in the actual etch-hollow, or an ancient unworkable stalk is sold as a new premium fiber crop.
A glower radius or sprite shrinks while its useful crop overlight and the nearby predator’s behavior remain unchanged.

A moth reaches a farm lamp and feeds; the productive lit edge contracts and an ishvarith can approach closer. The colony excludes the feeder, usable light returns and the approaching predator retreats toward reachable darkness.
A moth feeding through a sealed wall darkens a safe room, or removing it resets the ambient Dark and another mod’s light contribution.
A moth outside a sealed lamp room cannot feed through its wall; a tamed moth still flies but leaves the light alone.
Restored light claims an invulnerable camp although the cornered predator has no reachable escape.
A flying moth only walks with an animated texture, or expired animals are silently deleted to balance the population.
A tame utility animal exists in the def database but ordinary colony handling cannot obtain its advertised pack, milk or haul role.
A krizzak actually flies and later lands; death leaves a body and cause rather than a disappearing pawn, while native animal needs are met by the specified local resources.
A populated roster yields only starving dormant feeders and predators until the map is empty.

Gharreks open and feed with real gusts while ordinary native prey graze and predators leave a readable kill; aveluthia carry loads, milk stock produce food and trained sorters forage cleanables and haul.
Dust appears as decoration or a cheap def-count proof, but ordinary hauling/refining cannot use it; fuel stock grows without taking exposed material or work.
A water-rain event corrodes everything outside, wets growth-engine cells and harms animals while roofed steel still takes the same damage.
Natural rock eventually eaten away leaves a true hollow that admits etchcap, while an equally fertile plain-sand control does not.

Matched exposed and roofed steel work diverge under grain: the exposed work wears, the roofed work is spared, and collected tholin refines through an ordinary bill into fuel usable for ordinary warmth.
Stone furniture and all neighboring terrain vanish together as though they were natural rock.
A low-pass filter affects every interface alarm and other maps regardless of where the listener is, or silence removes the close danger tell.
The same map sound is muffled with the camera in Dark and becomes clearer in a warm pocket; gust impact and feeding rustle follow the actual wind pulse and grain ticks identify exposed work.
A close predator’s text tell and the interface remain readable while environmental sound is muffled, and a quiet map does not keep playing an unrelated steady wind bed.
A forced gust counter produces impressive sound while natural wind remains steady and no ordinary animal feeding pulse occurs.

A save made during active light/air/material pressure resumes into the same kind of recoverable routine; planting before heating and heating before planting both reach usable work when their ordinary prerequisites are met.

During routine residence, workers roof and heat a refuge, maintain a living-light farm, handle a local feeder failure and use recovered grain; native life continues and the explored country periodically clears and closes.
The main work sequence succeeds only in its scripted order because warming, planting or excluding a feeder leaves stale state in another system.
A staged clearing with fire, predation or grain switched off looks successful, but full default play empties the native food chain or eats the colony’s land.
Residue fills paths and storage without useful cost, light failures require continual bespoke intervention, ordinary work cannot resume, or a mid-cycle reload starts repeated exceptions.

rounds.missed_capability: The Witchfire storm weather itself (RM_AbyssWitchfire in Defs/WeatherDefs/RM_Weathers_Abyss.xml: wind multiplier, lightning, keeps the Dark, map-wide accuracy penalty), and the RM_AbyssDark weather def as a weather, have no census row. Witchfire is folded into the storm_call row, which goes to next_version, and only that row's 'why' says Witchfire weather stays. Yet B1/B2/B5/B8 ranges, R5 (the ambiguities say 'Witchfire multiplies wind', which gust feeding depends on) and the worst-day story all rely on it. T3's switch-off could therefore be built to suppress the weather along with the call.
rounds.loop_or_three_way: Heat closes a three-way meeting between B3, B4 and R4 that the 'light grid' meeting doesn't list, because R1 and the feeding temperature cutoff are not members. The Dark clears fully at 14 °C (RM_AbyssKernel.cs:21-22, ClearFull = 14). Krizzaks stop feeding above 35 °C (RM_CompKrizzak.cs:22,41, maxFeedTemperature 35). Ordinary crops keep growing well above 35 °C [guess ~80%: vanilla's growth curve runs to about 42 °C]. So a heated farm held between the cutoff and the crop limit clears the Dark (B2/R1), grows crops under living light (B3) and permanently bars every krizzak (R4) with one thermostat. Then B4's 'until they are excluded' and B8's 'handle a local feeder failure' never happen in ordinary play, and the signature's threat leg disappears without any bar failing.

refusals.head: contradicts_ruling_or_lore
refusals.where: definition.md 'Physical boundaries and transitions'; bars.json R1 and B1; next_version.md 'outdoor drifting pockets'; owner_pages.md page two
refusals.evidence: The frozen sheet design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/abyss.md §5 'Always true' says: 'The Dark is present, material, and temperature-structured; clear pockets are real, sharp-edged, and unexplained to everyone in-world.' §1 says it 'parts without warning into pockets of impossibly clear air'. The proposal removes every outdoor pocket for 0.1.0. R1 says 'no outdoor microclimate is promised', so clear air exists only inside heated rooms, which a heater explains, or map-wide through Unveiling or a change in the shared outdoor temperature, which is not a pocket. Page two lists this only as a default ('Clear edges are heated doorways, not spontaneous outdoor pockets'). It never says the change breaks an Always-true lore line, and result.json reports questions: 0.
refusals.would_pass: Either keep sharp-edged, unexplained outdoor clear pockets in 0.1.0 as part of the signature, with a definition and a bar picture, or state on his pages that the lore and the engine conflict. That statement names the §5 line, the engine fact that RimWorld has one outdoor temperature (so 'only a thermometer can tell' cannot hold literally), and the default taken. It is asked as a question carrying that evidence, as brief step 4 and the Evidence-for-Ask rule require.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add one question to owner_pages.md page two: the §5 'clear pockets are real' line against the single outdoor temperature, the default (no outdoor pockets in 0.1.0, built offset off under T43), and what changes if he says keep them (T43 becomes a signature item and B1 gains an outdoor pocket picture). Set result.json questions to 1.

refusals.head: kept_mechanic_undefined
refusals.where: census.json row dark_optical_paths (built: absent, fate: signature, ticket T31); bars.json B2 says and R2; tickets.md T31
refusals.evidence: This kept signature mechanic is unbuilt and only stated in outline. R2 says 'clear endpoints do not bypass intervening Dark'. T31 says 'rays through outdoor Dark remain obstructed'. B2 says 'a clear position cannot grant clean sight'. ambiguities.md leaves the 'sampling algorithm' as an attackable rule. Nothing says what obstruction does to a shot. It could lower hit chance by the density along the path, cap the range, or block targeting entirely. Nothing says whether raiders, turrets and animals are affected the same way as colonists. Nothing says what happens when B1's still-visible dim silhouette can or cannot be ordered attacked. 'Clean' is unmarked, so a token 1% penalty passes B2 as written.
refusals.would_pass: R2 or definition.md states the form of the effect. For example: accumulated Dark along the line lowers sight and hit chance the way vanilla weather accuracy does; it never removes the target from selection; it applies to every shooter, raiders and turrets included. B2 gains a reject picture that separates a negligible path penalty from real obstruction, without pinning a number.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add one sentence to R2 naming the effect form and who it applies to, and add one B2 reject picture: 'intervening Dark costs a long shot almost nothing compared with the same shot through clear air'.

refusals.head: figurative_unmarked
refusals.where: bars.json B2 says ('A visitor in the Abyss loses usable sight and aim')
refusals.evidence: B1 says, R2 and definition.md use 'neutral visitors' to mean pawns of other factions, as distinct from colonists. B2 uses 'visitor' for whoever carries murk. The census row 'murk' gives that as every humanlike: 'Humanlike sight/aim/melee hediff follows local Dark'. abyss.md §2 uses 'visitors' to mean outsiders, the colony included. B2's figurative list is empty, so a builder who applies murk only to neutral guest pawns passes B2 by the B1 meaning.
refusals.would_pass: B2 names its subject literally (a colonist or any other non-native humanlike), or marks 'visitor' as figurative with what it stands for and an accept picture showing a colonist impaired.
refusals.smallest_fix: Change B2 says to 'A colonist or other non-native pawn in the Abyss loses…', or add {word: 'visitor', stands_for: 'every non-native humanlike, colonists included'} to B2 meant.figurative.

refusals.head: evidence_cannot_tell
refusals.evidence: B3 says native food, grazing, timber and fiber plants 'persist without real sky light'. The control lists only 'Fertility, artificial sunlamps or inventory injections' and 'remove other glowers'. It never records or excludes sky glow. No Abyss source touches sky glow (searched [measured]: only RM_CompSummHide reads skyManager.CurSkyGlow, and it expects it to reach 0.5 'under bright open sky'). B1's range assumes 'day/night palette slots for the same fixed solar geometry'. So on any map whose solar geometry gives daytime sky glow, a native plant kept alive by daylight passes the 'persist without real sky light' reading. Abyss sheet §6 ban 6 ('No sun-dependent resident life') is exactly that false pass.
refusals.would_pass: The B3 instrument records the sky-glow contribution at every sampled plant and plot. Persistence and establishment are read with sky glow attributed or excluded, for example night-phase readings or growth eligibility traced to glow source, so daylight cannot stand in for living light.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add to B3 sees.control: 'record sky/sun glow at each sample; a native plant counts as persisting without sky light only where its growth eligibility holds with the sky contribution removed'.

refusals.head: core_promise_weakened
refusals.where: owner_pages.md line 13; definition.md 'Why a player reaches for it'; bars.json B1 and B8 meant
refusals.evidence: His 2026-10-20 experience (design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md): 'Wonders emerge just as often for moments of transcendent beauty, only to twist into nightmares just as swiftly.' The proposal defers 'the swift twist into nightmares' 'with cryptid content'. Yet the kept mechanics already make that turn. Unveiling (the wonder, B1) ends, the Dark returns (R1), lamps shrink (R3), krizzaks feed (B4) and the ishvarith closes in as light fails (B4). That is a 'terror close by' with no cryptid system. No bar or picture asks for that sequence, so a build where Unveiling's end changes nothing nearby passes every bar. The clause is dropped without an argument that the kept mechanics cannot carry it.
refusals.would_pass: An accept picture in B8 or B1 in which Unveiling's close readably brings nearby danger back to the colony's edge through the kept Dark, light and predator chain, with a reject picture where the clearing ends and nothing nearby changes. Alternatively, an argument with evidence for why the kept chain cannot carry the clause.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add one accept and one reject picture to B8 (no new system), and narrow the page-one deferral to the source-of-nightmares dread only.

rounds.missed_capability: Player wind power under gust-only wind. abyss.md §5 lists among its Always-true lines 'Wind-grasping technology breaks often — the Dark fouls it and the gust-shear snaps it; repair is a way of life', and §6 ban 2 forbids steady wind. The census has no row for what a vanilla wind turbine the player builds does on an Abyss map. Under R5's single real wind history it either produces steady power, which would show that ban 2 is violated, or produces pulses, or breaks. That also feeds B8's warmth economy (electric heaters running on wind as an alternative to tholin fuel). Only the inert wreck field and the cut gust-turbine echo are covered; the playable vanilla turbine is not.
rounds.loop_or_three_way: Sky glow, light aversion and the Dark meet three ways, and no meeting lists them together. CompLightAversion flees only when map.glowGrid.PsychGlowAt reads Dark (RM_CompLightAversion.cs:57,63). The Dark field changes glower radii through the ledger (R3) but never sky glow (no Abyss source touches it [measured]). R12 and Direct Sun keep solar geometry untouched, and B1 assumes a day/night cycle. If the tile's daytime or Unveiling sky glow lifts outdoor PsychGlow above Dark [guess ~50%, unmeasured], the ishvarith has no reachable darkness. R4 then forbids its retreat, so restored lamp light stops deterring it (B4 fails). Or it flees continually, emptying predation (B5/B8). Either way the colony's lamp stops being what decides. The 'light grid' meeting (B1–B4, B8, R3, R4, R9) and the 'weather and gust' meeting never join the sky, map time and aversion; M3 should sweep sky glow by solar phase and weather alongside glower shares.

The census row 'murk' gives that as every humanlike: 'Humanlike sight/aim/melee hediff follows local Dark'. abyss.md §2 uses 'visitors' to mean outsiders, the colony included. B2's figurative list is empty, so a builder who applies murk only to neutral guest pawns passes B2 by the B1 meaning.
remaining.would_pass: B2 names its subject literally (a colonist or any other non-native humanlike), or marks 'visitor' as figurative with what it stands for and an accept picture showing a colonist impaired.
remaining.smallest_fix: Change B2 says to 'A colonist or other non-native pawn in the Abyss loses…', or add {word: 'visitor', stands_for: 'every non-native humanlike, colonists included'} to B2 meant.figurative.

remaining.head: evidence_cannot_tell
remaining.evidence: B3 says native food, grazing, timber and fiber plants 'persist without real sky light'. The control lists only 'Fertility, artificial sunlamps or inventory injections' and 'remove other glowers'. It never records or excludes sky glow. No Abyss source touches sky glow (searched [measured]: only RM_CompSummHide reads skyManager.CurSkyGlow, and it expects it to reach 0.5 'under bright open sky'). B1's range assumes 'day/night palette slots for the same fixed solar geometry'. So on any map whose solar geometry gives daytime sky glow, a native plant kept alive by daylight passes the 'persist without real sky light' reading. Abyss sheet §6 ban 6 ('No sun-dependent resident life') is exactly that false pass.
remaining.would_pass: The B3 instrument records the sky-glow contribution at every sampled plant and plot. Persistence and establishment are read with sky glow attributed or excluded, for example night-phase readings or growth eligibility traced to glow source, so daylight cannot stand in for living light.
remaining.smallest_fix: Add to B3 sees.control: 'record sky/sun glow at each sample; a native plant counts as persisting without sky light only where its growth eligibility holds with the sky contribution removed'.

remaining.head: core_promise_weakened
remaining.where: owner_pages.md line 13; definition.md 'Why a player reaches for it'; bars.json B1 and B8 meant
remaining.evidence: His 2026-10-20 experience (design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md): 'Wonders emerge just as often for moments of transcendent beauty, only to twist into nightmares just as swiftly.' The proposal defers 'the swift twist into nightmares' 'with cryptid content'. Yet the kept mechanics already make that turn. Unveiling (the wonder, B1) ends, the Dark returns (R1), lamps shrink (R3), krizzaks feed (B4) and the ishvarith closes in as light fails (B4). That is a 'terror close by' with no cryptid system. No bar or picture asks for that sequence, so a build where Unveiling's end changes nothing nearby passes every bar. The clause is dropped without an argument that the kept mechanics cannot carry it.
remaining.would_pass: An accept picture in B8 or B1 in which Unveiling's close readably brings nearby danger back to the colony's edge through the kept Dark, light and predator chain, with a reject picture where the clearing ends and nothing nearby changes. Alternatively, an argument with evidence for why the kept chain cannot carry the clause.
remaining.smallest_fix: Add one accept and one reject picture to B8 (no new system), and narrow the page-one deferral to the source-of-nightmares dread only.
